title: studio(actions): switching an action to "Run a script" writes a body the spec refuses until a language is picked by hand — commitOperation seeds no body, and patchBody writes no language
body:
Filing gate: ① product defect, class (a), reach by a named producer, measured. Studio's own action inspector (`ActionDefaultInspector`) writes the refused shapes. Since objectui#11820 (PR objectui#11918), a new action starts as an update action, so "What it does: Run a script" is the path for every author who wants a script action. Reader: objectui triage first-touch (grade and route).

Dedupe (MCP `search_issues`, objectui, open + closed):
- "action switched to run a script refused body language missing commitOperation seeds no body" returned objectui#2896 and #2904 (closed; the runner's handling of `action.body`). Neither is this.
- Positive control, same run: "studio risky no-op defaults new action sandboxed JS hook all objects validation rule" returned objectui#11820: yes.

Filed by the `domain:ui` execution seat 3 (`session_01CGZy1BGCjdN5cXqL9cnvB8`) from the objectui#11820 dev report (`6053900490`, out-of-scope finding 1, and its open question 2, answered "file it, let objectui#11820 land"). ⛔ Not graded or routed here; ⛔ not a claim.

## What happens (measured through the spec's `ActionSchema` on the shapes the inspector writes)

In `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/ActionDefaultInspector.tsx` (objectui `main` `3683591`):
- `commitOperation` clears `operation` / `patch` when the author picks "Run a script", and seeds no `body`. `ActionSchema` refuses the result at `body`: "A script action requires either an inline body … or a target".
- `patchBody` writes `{ source }` as the author types, with no `language`. `ActionSchema` refuses it at `body.language`: "Invalid discriminator value. Expected 'expression' | 'js'".
- It parses only after the author explicitly picks a language (for example *Sandboxed JS (L2)*).

## Done when

- Switching an action to a script writes a body `ActionSchema` parses, with a seeded language, so the first keystroke is not refused.
- A pin parses each shape the inspector writes through `ActionSchema`: after the switch, after the first keystroke, and after a language change.

Dedupe words: action what it does run a script body language refused · commitOperation seeds no body · update action switch to script
